method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Customs Act 1901, compilation register id C2026C00378, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/C1901A00006.txt (retrieved 2026-09-22); with the Customs Regulation 2015, Compilation No. 38, compilation date 1 July 2026 (register id F2026C00589; regs 25-27A, 133, Schedule 8), the Customs Tariff Act 1995, register id C2026C00399 (Schedule 4 item 15, s 18), and the Crimes Act 1914 s 4AA (register id C2026C00368), as deposited in their own subject folders; the Customs By-laws and the Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 are not deposited and their content is an input

checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: From the seat of the incoming traveller. Personal effects and the entry duty (s 68(1)(d), (3), (4); regs 25-26, $1 000); the incoming passenger card: when a Collector's request makes it due, and the Australia Travel Declaration alternative (ss 71, 71AAAA, 71AAAB; regs 27(3), (6), 27A(2)(b)); the card's questions and thresholds (reg 27(2)(e)-(i): 2,250 mL, 25 cigarettes or 25 g, $900 or $450 for crew, prohibited goods, samples); the passenger concession (Customs Tariff Sch 4 item 15, s 18) with the By-law figures as inputs; prohibited imports (ss 50-51) and forfeiture (s 229(1)(a), (b), (q)); questions to passengers (s 195); false statements (s 234(1)(d), (2)(c), (3); ss 243T, 243U, including the passenger exclusion in s 243U(5)(b), error notices and uncertainty statements); infringement notices (s 243X; reg 133; Sch 8); smuggling (s 4(1), s 233(1)(a), (b), s 233AB), evading duty (s 234(1)(a)) and tobacco fraud (s 233BABAD). Not encoded: cargo, post and commercial entries; duty rates; the By-laws' treatment of goods over the concession; tier 1 and 2, narcotic and restricted goods; search and seizure; prosecution; the outgoing traveller; the Biosecurity Act declaration on the same card.
